newsitem.title: USA: CBOT August soybeans up sharply on strong cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT August soybeans up sharply on strong cash.

text.p: CBOT August soybean futures were sharply higher in early trade on short covering ahead of expiration amid strong cash basis levels in the country and at the U.S. Gulf, traders said.

"We thought the deliveries would take some steam out of the August," a trader said. "But the basis is up and there's talk that six boats are waiting to load soybeans (out of the Great Lakes) and they can't get the beans."
Cash basis levels in the country were up 10 to 15 cents per bushel at several Illinois, Indiana and Iowa locations, cash sources said. U.S. Gulf CIF values were also higher.
There were 40,000 bushels of soybeans posted for delivery against the August on Thursday.
Pit sources said locals and commission houses were light buyers of the August. They cited short covering ahead of expiration on August 20.
CBOT said the preliminary open interest in the August stood at 28.97 million bushels as of August 13, down 6.345 million from the previous day.
At 1050 CDT, soybeans were up 11 cents per bushel to down 3-1/2 cents with August up 11 at $7.90 a bushel.
